scene.testo: This is Giovanna. Her cardiology report has just landed in her electronic health record, weeks before she can talk to her doctor. She reads it once. Then again. And one question remains: what does it mean? She is not alone. <break time="1.2s" /> More than half of Italians struggle to make sense of health information. So they search online, ask a chatbot, or call a family doctor who is already overloaded.

scene.testo: Giovanna ha appena fatto una visita cardiologica, e il referto è già nel portale del suo poliambulatorio. Un clic su «Spiegamelo», e Referto si mette al lavoro. Prima arriva la sintesi, poi la spiegazione in parole semplici, mentre viene scritta. Le indicazioni del medico restano in un riquadro a parte, sempre attribuite al documento. E se il referto lascia qualcosa in sospeso, Referto lo dice chiaramente.
scene.inglese: Giovanna opens her clinic's portal, and her report is already there. One click on Explain this to me, and Referto gets to work: first a summary, then a plain explanation, written in real time. The doctor's instructions stay in a separate box, linked to the original document. And if the report leaves questions open, Referto says so.

scene.testo: Giovanna ha ancora un dubbio, e lo chiede con parole sue: cos'è il ritmo sinusale? La risposta arriva dal glossario medico, con la sua fonte.
scene.inglese: Still have a question? Giovanna can ask in her own words. For instance, what is a sinus rhythm? The answer is provided via a medical glossary, complete with its source. <break time="1.0s" />

scene.testo: Nel referto c'è un farmaco: il ramipril. Referto lo trova nel prontuario ufficiale dell'AIFA, e apre il foglietto illustrativo, dove Giovanna può fare le sue domande. Il medico chiede una nuova visita cardiologica? Ecco le strutture di cardiologia più vicine, sulla mappa.
scene.inglese: Does the report mention a medication, such as ramipril? Referto locates it in the official AIFA, Italian Medicines Agency database, and opens the patient information leaflet, where Giovanna can ask her own questions, like what it is for. The answer comes straight from the leaflet, with the section where to find it. <break time="1.0s" /> Does the doctor recommend a follow-up cardiology appointment? Referto displays the nearest cardiology clinics, with the distance from her home, and shows each one on a map. <break time="2.5s" />

scene.testo: Dietro le quinte, un agente legge il referto, e consulta il prontuario dell'AIFA e il glossario medico. Le strutture sanitarie arrivano dai dati aperti, a partire dall'area del referto. E il modello linguistico gira su infrastruttura A M D, con A M D Token Factory.
scene.inglese: Behind the scenes, an AI agent reads the report and checks the AIFA database and a medical glossary. Healthcare facilities come from open data, based on the medical specialty in the report. The language model runs on AMD infrastructure, with AMD Token Factory. <break time="1.5s" />

scene.testo: And every run leaves a trace: timings, tokens, the tools the agent called, and the outcome. Never the text of the report. We use these traces to measure every version of Referto, and to make the next one better.

scene.testo: The timing is right. Since 2026, every report in Italy must reach the electronic health record within five days. The country invested 1.38 billion euros in it, yet only one in four Italians uses it. That is our market: Italian digital health, worth 2.7 billion euros a year and growing. Referto plugs into the portals that deliver reports: doctors' practices first, like Giovanna's, then labs, then every region's health record. And with the European Health Data Space, the same need reaches 450 million Europeans.
